what: Paccar builds heavy trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF brands, and makes its own engines. It also sells parts through a large dealer network and runs a finance arm that lends to truck buyers.
customers: Truck fleets, owner-operators and leasing companies in North America, Europe and Australia.
money: Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF heavy and medium trucks
loans and leases to truck buyers
moat: Premium brands that hold resale value, a dealer network owner-operators rely on, and a parts business that earns money for the twenty-year life of each truck.
risks: Truck orders fell sharply last year and revenue dropped about 16%
Freight rates and trucking profitability drive demand
Emission rule changes pull demand forward and then leave a gap
Tariffs raise the cost of imported components
opportunities: Parts revenue holds up when new truck sales fall, cushioning the cycle
Almost no debt at the industrial company, with return on invested capital near 12%
Analysts see about 20% upside, with a cyclical recovery expected
watch: North American Class 8 truck orders and parts revenue growth.
